EngineInfo.description:
What one replica says about itself, read best effort: runtime information, never part of an identity.

Read from the standard ``GET <base_url>/models`` (the entry of the served model) and the response headers,
and from the ``system_fingerprint`` of the replica's first completion; nothing engine-specific is asked.

error.description: Why the endpoint could not be read; the other fields are then empty.
error.title: Error

headers.description: The response's ``server`` header and any header naming a version.
headers.title: Headers

max_model_len.description: The served context in tokens, when the endpoint reports it.
max_model_len.title: Max Model Len

model.description: The served model id the endpoint lists (the judge's ``model`` when listed, else the first).
model.title: Model

owned_by.description: The entry's ``owned_by``; open-source engines put their own name there.
owned_by.title: Owned By

system_fingerprint.description: The ``system_fingerprint`` of the first completion, when the endpoint sends one (some engines put their version in it).
system_fingerprint.title: System Fingerprint

url.description: The replica's base URL, with any userinfo and query stripped (a key in a URL never reaches the record beside the code's never-logged claim).
url.title: Url

EngineInfo.title: EngineInfo

Family.description:
The poolability token of a set of judgements.

Two judgements measure the same thing -- and may enter one fit -- only when
every field matches: the stage, the judge (model, checkpoint and tokenizer), the prompt,
the criteria, the parser, the decoding and the preprocessing that shaped
what the judge saw. key digests them; rubric_key leaves out the judge, which
is the precondition for pooling several judges with a severity term.

api.description: The judge's wire adapter name, when the pass was given one other than its default wire (the judging pass normalizes the default wire's own name away, so families judged on the default keep their key whatever its spelling).
api.title: Api

context_tokens.description: The judge's prompt-plus-completion budget (the window text budget's basis), when declared.
context_tokens.title: Context Tokens

criteria.description: The rubric's criterion labels (``C1..C5``); empty for the tournament.
criteria.title: Criteria

decoding.description: ``"json_schema"`` when the endpoint was made to answer in the stage's JSON schema, ``"free"`` when it answered in free text (Decoding).
decoding.title: Decoding

extra_body.description: The judge's extra request fields, when any are declared.
extra_body.title: Extra Body

judge_model.description: The served model name (``"fake"`` for the offline fake judge).
judge_model.title: Judge Model

judge_revision.description: The judge config's ``revision`` as configured (not resolved against the Hub), or ``None``.
judge_revision.title: Judge Revision

max_output_tokens.description: The judge's completion-token cap per request, when declared.
max_output_tokens.title: Max Output Tokens

parse_version.description: Version of the parser that reads the answers.
parse_version.title: Parse Version

preprocessing.description: Digest of the effective preprocessing policy (text caps, chunking, image and video policies), or ``None`` when nothing was declared.
preprocessing.title: Preprocessing

prompt_hash.description: SHA-256 of the prompt template text.
prompt_hash.title: Prompt Hash

temperature.description: The judge's sampling temperature, when it declared one (``None``: the server's default applies, and the field stays out of the digest).
temperature.title: Temperature

tokenizer.description: SHA-256 of the judge's ``tokenizer.json``, in whose tokens the text limits and the window budget were counted, or ``None`` when the judge names no tokenizer. It is the judge's, so rubric_key leaves it out with the model.
tokenizer.title: Tokenizer

Family.title: Family

StageEntry.description:
One stage's entry in a store's ``identity.json``: the identity its judgements answer for, and when and by
what it was claimed.

created_at.description: When the stage was claimed (ISO 8601, UTC).
created_at.title: Created At

engines.description: What the endpoints said they serve, one entry per distinct report (runtime information, never part of the identity).
engines.title: Engines

family.description: The family of the stage's judgements.

identity.description: The identity of the judging pass that writes the stage; a later pass into the store is compared with it field by field. Its keys: ``stage``, ``family`` (the Family), ``judge`` (the judge config's content fields), ``schedule`` (its numbers; the prompt is the family's ``prompt_hash``), ``dataset`` (its name, and for a loaded dataset its URI, local paths absolute, and resolved revision), ``preprocessing`` (the effective policy, with the tokenizer's SHA-256), and for the tournament ``bt_l2`` (the penalty of the live Bradley-Terry fit that chose its adaptive windows). Only content enters it: the names the inputs were given are ``sources``.
identity.title: Identity

package_version.description: The rcp-ndcg version that claimed it.
package_version.title: Package Version

sources.description: How the claiming pass named its inputs: ``prompt`` (the prompt's name or path), ``schedule_prompt`` (the schedule's ``prompt``, which JudgementStore.schedule gives back) and ``tokenizer`` (as the judge config named it). Runtime information, never compared.
sources.title: Sources

StageEntry.title: StageEntry

description: ``identity.json`` of a judgement store (``rcp-ndcg.judgement-store.v1``): an entry per stage it holds.

stages.description: ``{stage: StageEntry}`` for each stage written into the store.
stages.title: Stages
